title: Bengaluru eyewear D2C lifted try-at-home conversion 18% → 31% by unifying online+offline on one phone number, not adding channels
content: A Bengaluru eyewear D2C (7 stores across Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Pune; Shopify + Amazon.in) ran a 5-frame 'try-at-home' kit and spent ₹9L/month on Meta and Google, booking 2,400 try-at-home requests/month but converting only 18% (~432 sales). The leak was structural: a customer who tried frames at home, then walked into a store, was logged as a fresh 'new walk-in' — staff re-pitched, handed out a second discount, and the ₹480 two-way reverse-logistics cost per kit was never recovered. Online ran on Shopify, stores on a separate POS-CRM, and nobody owned the end-to-end journey, so the same buyer was acquired and discounted twice. We made the phone number the single customer key via the WhatsApp Business API: every try-at-home booking fired a WhatsApp flow, and store staff scanned that same number at billing, collapsing online and walk-in into one record. Non-converters were retargeted on Meta and Instagram with the exact frame they had kept longest in the kit, and tier-2 requests (Pune, Nashik, Mysuru) were routed to nearest-store pickup to kill two-way courier cost. Over 4 months, try-at-home conversion rose 18% → 31% (~744 sales/month), blended CAC fell ₹1,240 → ₹860, reverse-logistics spend dropped 38%, and the unified WhatsApp journey drove ₹22L in incremental revenue at a ₹2.4L all-in cost.
lesson: Omnichannel is not more channels — it is one identity. Until offline and online share a single customer key (the phone number is the only one every Indian buyer already carries), you pay to acquire the same person twice and discount them again at the counter, so spend looks efficient per-channel while blended CAC bleeds. Unify the ID first, then optimise spend: in eyewear, beauty, and any try-before-buy D2C, the cheapest 'new' conversion is the buyer you already half-acquired but failed to recognise.
